sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to as per their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the petitioners' case are that on 19th January, 2017 at 11.00 am on Belagavi-Bagalkot road near the land of Hoovappa Katnaik situate within the limits of Budigoppa village, when the deceased Hanumanta Erappa Uppar was proceeding from Lakkundi to Yakkundi on his Bajaj motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-23/ED-3473 along with his mother Renavva and mother of petitioners in MVC 1104 No.2017 Yamanava Uppar, at that time, driver of the truck bearing Registration No.AP-16/TY-7733 came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle in which the rider and pillion riders were travelling, and caused the accident.
The rider and both pillion riders NC: 2023:KHC-D:10939-DB C/W MFA No. 101541 of 2021, succumbed to the accidental injuries.
Thereafter dead bodies of the deceased were shifted to Government Hospital, Yaragatti and after conducting post-mortem, the bodies were handed over to the petitioners.
Further, it is stated as to the loss of dependency, earnings of the deceased, etc. and sought for compensation.
4. In pursuance of notice issued, respondents 1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed objections.

The substance of objection of respondent No.1 is that as on the date of the accident,
respondent No.1 was the owner-cum- driver of the truck and was driving the truck in a moderate speed by observing traffic rules and due to the wrong act of the rider of the motorcycle, the accident had taken place.
As the on the date of accident, the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.
There is no breach of terms and conditions of policy.

If the court comes to conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for compensation, then the liability may be saddled on respondent No.2 and accordingly, sought dismissal of claim petition against him.
The substance of written statement of respondent No.2 is that the driver of truck violated the terms and conditions of insurance policy.
Driver of the truck was using the vehicle against the policy conditions.

As per charge sheet filed by the jurisdictional police for offence punishable under Section 304(ii) of Indian Penal Code, thereby it shows that the driver of the truck unintentionally causes death and there is no negligent act, therefore, petitions filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are not maintainable.

It is further contended that as on the date of accident, deceased who was riding the motorcycle with two pillion riders has lost control and dashed to the truck and hence the accident took place on the negligent act of the deceased.
Hence the petitioners are not entitled to claim compensation against the Insurance company.

It is further contended that the driver and respondent No.1 have contravened the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 since the driver of the truck was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the owner of the vehicle has handed over the vehicle to a person who was not holding valid and effective driving licence.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Learned counsel for the insurance company has submitted that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased rider of the motorcycle.
The document on record, especially exhibits P4 and P5, reveals the same.
Even then the Court below has saddled the entire liability on the appellant- Insurance Company.
The police have charge-sheeted the driver of the truck under Section 304(ii) of Indian Penal Code and not under Section 304A of the Indian Penal Code.

At the time of accident, the rider was riding the motorcycle with two pillion riders which is against the provisions of Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the same has not at all been considered by the Tribunal.
It is excellent requirement to file charge sheet against the offending vehicle under Section 279, 304A of Indian Penal Code but the same is not complied with.
Learned counsel further submits that the Tribunal has awarded higher compensation, which is contrary to law and facts.

The learned counsel further submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding exorbitant interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation which - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10939-DB C/W MFA No. 101541 of 2021, needs to be reduced.
On all these grounds, sought to allow the appeals.

8. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-claimants submits that the Tribunal has rightly held that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
He further submits that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation in accordance with law and facts and also the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court.

Learned Counsel submits that though the claimants have not preferred any appeal for enhancement of compensation,
this Court can award the compensation invoking provisions under Order XLI Rule 33 of Code of Civil Procedure and accordingly, sought for dismissal of appeals filed by the insurance company and to enhance the compensation.

12. On perusal of material placed before this Court, we are of the considered view that the petitioners have proved that the deceased died in the motor vehicle accident.

The main argument advanced on behalf the learned counsel for the insurance company is that the Investigating Officer has not submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for commission of offence punishable under Sections 279 and 304A of Indian Penal Code and therefore, claim petitions are not maintainable.

This argument advanced on behalf of the Insurance Company cannot be accepted for the reason that the material placed before this Court clearly depicts that the deceased died due to motor vehicle accident.

Though the Investigating Officer has submitted the charge sheet under Section 304(ii) of the Indian Penal Code instead of Sections 279 and 304A, the same cannot be a ground for rejection of claim petition filed by the petitioners.

The Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record and come to the conclusion that the petitioners have proved that the accident occurred due - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10939-DB C/W MFA No. 101541 of 2021, to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the truck.

The another defence set up by the Insurance Company is that three persons were proceeding on the motorcycle which is offence under Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 and hence they are not entitled for any compensation towards loss of dependency.
To substantiate this, respondents have not placed any material before this Court.

Even if it is presumed that the rider of the motorcycle has committed offence under Section 128 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, that itself is not sufficient to come to the conclusion that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by its rider.

Investigating Officer has not made any accusation against the rider of the motorcycle for the commission of offence under Section 128 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 or under Sections 279 and 304A of Indian Penal Code.
